No extraction parameters changed based on these examples.

findings: No proposed sequence longer than five tokens matched the corpus. Attention method proposes only pairs, so it cannot test passage extraction.
The 504 real MLP paths with at least four matching tokens collapse to 17 distinct selected longest substrings, mostly punctuation and whitespace formatting.
Matched trained attention pairs exceed a broken-head control and the step-10 checkpoint, but frequency and source-selection effects remain confounds.
Global vocabulary-label permutation does not preserve token frequencies and is only a diagnostic negative control.

HF tokenizer.json produced 1,836,425 tokens; the native training tokenizer produced 1,835,163. All authoritative results below use the native export with every token byte interval checked. The earlier HF report is superseded, not deleted.
purpose: Corpus-blind static weight extraction, independently verified against native training tokens. No model inference. Learned associations are not proof of passage memorization or compression.
